newsitem.title: FRANCE: French CFDT union points to pay in workweek debate.
newsitem.headline: French CFDT union points to pay in workweek debate.

text.p: The leader of France's large CFDT union, Nicole Notat, said in an interview published on Friday that she backed the idea of a shorter work week but feared that cutting hours without cutting pay would fail to create jobs.
New Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has set a goal of reducing the work week to 35 hours over the next three years.
Notat, who is carving herself a strategy of consensual union boss, said earlier this week she wanted the shift to a shorter work week to be carefully prepared and negotiated.
She told the Friday edition of daily Liberation the one-hour cut in the past, to a current 39-hour work week, failed to produce jobs.

"The change to 39 hours from 40 hours without loss of salary created zero employment," she said. "I fear and in fact I'm sure that a phased shift to 35 from 39 without loss of salary will have the same effect," she said.
"It is necessary to leave a margin of freedom to the social partners and negotiate it," she said.

Notat said she was in favour of increasing the SMIC minimum wage but warned, as has the Force Ouvriere union, that there was also a danger in the SMIC, because hiking it also increased the number of people who paid less social security contributions.
She also called for a rethink of the contribution system to prevent companies who employ many people from bearing the brunt of financing of unemployment.
Notat said that she was not against privatisations.

"We are in an ideological debate between privatisations and nationalisations which often leads people to forget what the real issue is. The question is to know whether it is necessary to put in place an industrial policy which includes alliances, to privatise or not and to what extent," she said.

"The fact that Renault, for example, did not open its capital in 1993 has evidently been an obstacle for its alliance with Volvo. That failure is weighing heavily on the company at the moment," Notat said.
